newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht weaker late, interbank rate steady.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht weaker late, interbank rate steady.

text.p: The Thai baht fell against the dollar in late slow trade on Friday in the domestic market on high commercial demand for the dollar, dealers said.
They said the recent turmoil in other regional currencies had a limited impact on onshore dollar/baht trade as most of the dollar buying today came from importers and borrowers of foreign loans.

"I think the volatility in other regional currencies affected (the dollar/baht) offshore rather than in the local market. Most trade today was really corporate demand," said one dealer at a major local bank.
The baht was quoted at 31.75/31.85 to the dollar late in onshore market compared with 31.60/31.70 in early trade.
Dealers said the market had ignored news of a cabinet reshuffle because the move was viewed as cosmetic.
In offshore market, the baht fell to 31.70/31.90 late from 31.60/31.70 in the morning.
"There was some spillover from the rupiah. But the liquidity is really thin which make it easier to move the market," said one dealer in Singapore.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was at 15/18 satangs per dollar late in domestic market and 23/33 satangs in offshore market.
The overnight interbank rate eased slightly to 11.00-12.00 from 13.00 in early morning.
